1. This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 23.09.2014 passed by District Consumer Forum, Latur partly allowing complainant's claim in consumer complaint No.2/2014 directing appellant/opponent insurance company to pay to the complainant amount of insurance Rs.1 lakh, compensation Rs.3000/- towards mental agony and Rs.3000/- more towards cost of the proceedings.

2 F.A..No.:736/2014

(For the sake of brevity appellant Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company is hereinafter referred as opponent insurance company and respondents as the complainants)

2. Brief facts giving rise to this appeal are that:-

On 13.4.2013 Late Sharad who was the son of complainants died in motor-accident while driving motor-cycle bearing No.MH- 24/AC-3059 belonging to one Sandeep Uttamrao Kalse. The same motor-cycle was insured with the opponent insurance company having policy No. OG-13-2010-180-200005361 for the period from 14.12.2012 to 13.12.2013 covering risk of owner-driver to the tune of Rs.1 lakh. After death of Sharad his parents/complainants submitted insurance claim with the opponent insurance company but their claim came to be repudiated on the ground that as per terms and conditions of the policy only owner of the vehicle or his L.R.s only are entitled for insurance claim etc. Accordingly complainants were informed.

Therefore alleging deficiency in service on the part of opponent insurance company, complainants have filed consumer complaint claiming amount of insurance Rs.1 lakh, compensation Rs.5000/- each towards mental agony and Rs.5000/- more towards cost of the proceeding, total Rs.1,15,000/-.

3. In response to the complaint notice, opponent insurance company appeared before the Forum and by its written version resisted the complaint contending inter alia that it has rightly repudiated the complainant's claim as no risk of third person is covered under the policy. According to insurance company only owner or L.R.s of owner of the vehicle are entitled etc. It has denied all other adverse averments made by the complainants and submitted to dismiss the complaint.

2 F.A..No.:736/2014

(For the sake of brevity appellant Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company is hereinafter referred as opponent insurance company and respondents as the complainants)

2. Brief facts giving rise to this appeal are that:-

On 13.4.2013 Late Sharad who was the son of complainants died in motor-accident while driving motor-cycle bearing No.MH- 24/AC-3059 belonging to one Sandeep Uttamrao Kalse. Therefore alleging deficiency in service on the part of opponent insurance company, complainants have filed consumer complaint claiming amount of insurance Rs.1 lakh, compensation Rs.5000/- each towards mental agony and Rs.5000/- more towards cost of the proceeding, total Rs.1,15,000/-.

3. According to insurance company only owner or L.R.s of owner of the vehicle are entitled etc. It has denied all other adverse averments made by the complainants and submitted to dismiss the complaint.

3 F.A..No.:736/2014

4. On hearing both side and considering evidence on record District Consumer Forum held that driver of the vehicle is covered under the policy in question and opponent insurance company committed deficiency in service by repudiating complainant's claim. In keeping with these findings Dist.Consumer Forum has partly allowed the complainant's claim as noted above.

5. Feeling aggrieved by that judgment and order, opponent insurance company came to this Commission in appeal.

6. We heard learned counsel for both side and perused the written notes of argument submitted by them. We have also perused the copy of impugned judgment and order, copies of complaint , written version, and other documents.

7. Almost all the facts except the contention of opponent insurance company that only owner of the insured vehicle or his L.R.s are entitled to claim insurance etc. are not disputed. Therefore the crux in this matter is as to whether any third person driving insured vehicle is covered under the policy in question or not?

8. Mr.Sandeep Gaikwad advocate appearing for the opponent insurance company pointing out from the copy of insurance policy submitted that only registered owner-driver of the insured vehicle who is holding effective driving license is covered under the policy.

9. Per contra, it is submitted by Mr.S.T.Agrawal advocate appearing for the complainants that owner as well as any third person driving the insured vehicle holding effective driving license is covered under the policy. It is further submitted that undisputedly Late Sharad who was the son of complainants was holding effective driving license and therefore he was covered under the policy and accordingly District Consumer Forum has rightly held.

3 F.A..No.:736/2014

4. On hearing both side and considering evidence on record District Consumer Forum held that driver of the vehicle is covered under the policy in question and opponent insurance company committed deficiency in service by repudiating complainant's claim. In keeping with these findings Dist.Consumer Forum has partly allowed the complainant's claim as noted above.

6. We heard learned counsel for both side and perused the written notes of argument submitted by them. We have also perused the copy of impugned judgment and order, copies of complaint , written version, and other documents.

7. Almost all the facts except the contention of opponent insurance company that only owner of the insured vehicle or his L.R.s are entitled to claim insurance etc. are not disputed. Therefore the crux in this matter is as to whether any third person driving insured vehicle is covered under the policy in question or not?

8. Mr.Sandeep Gaikwad advocate appearing for the opponent insurance company pointing out from the copy of insurance policy submitted that only registered owner-driver of the insured vehicle who is holding effective driving license is covered under the policy.

9. Per contra, it is submitted by Mr.S.T.Agrawal advocate appearing for the complainants that owner as well as any third person driving the insured vehicle holding effective driving license is covered under the policy. It is further submitted that undisputedly Late Sharad who was the son of complainants was holding effective driving license and therefore he was covered under the policy and accordingly District Consumer Forum has rightly held.

3 F.A..No.:736/2014

4. On hearing both side and considering evidence on record District Consumer Forum held that driver of the vehicle is covered under the policy in question and opponent insurance company committed deficiency in service by repudiating complainant's claim. In keeping with these findings Dist.Consumer Forum has partly allowed the complainant's claim as noted above.

5. Feeling aggrieved by that judgment and order, opponent insurance company came to this Commission in appeal.

6. We heard learned counsel for both side and perused the written notes of argument submitted by them. We have also perused the copy of impugned judgment and order, copies of complaint , written version, and other documents.

7. Almost all the facts except the contention of opponent insurance company that only owner of the insured vehicle or his L.R.s are entitled to claim insurance etc. are not disputed. Therefore the crux in this matter is as to whether any third person driving insured vehicle is covered under the policy in question or not?

8. Mr.Sandeep Gaikwad advocate appearing for the opponent insurance company pointing out from the copy of insurance policy submitted that only registered owner-driver of the insured vehicle who is holding effective driving license is covered under the policy.

9. Per contra, it is submitted by Mr.S.T.Agrawal advocate appearing for the complainants that owner as well as any third person driving the insured vehicle holding effective driving license is covered under the policy. It is further submitted that undisputedly Late Sharad who was the son of complainants was holding effective driving license and therefore he was covered under the policy and accordingly District Consumer Forum has rightly held.

4 F.A..No.:736/2014

10. On perusal of copy of policy it manifests that owner as well as any person driving vehicle holding effective driving license is covered under the policy. Accordingly it is mentioned as the owner-driver of the vehicle. If really only owner of the insured vehicle was covered, then the word 'driver' should not have been mentioned. Accordingly District Consumer Forum has rightly held. Therefore submission made by counsel for appellant insurance company is being contrary to the terms and conditions of the policy, cannot be sustained.

11. Thus we have given our anxious thoughts to the facts of the case and argument advanced by counsel for both side and we find that District Consumer Forum has rightly allowed complainant's claim. We find no infirmity or illegality in the impugned judgment and order. Hence no interference is warranted.

12. In the result, appeal is being devoid of any merit deserves to be dismissed. Hence the following order. 

                               O   R     D   E   R


   1. Appeal is dismissed.

2. Opponent insurance company shall pay to the complainant amount of Rs.3000/- towards cost of appeal proceeding and bear its own cost.

3. Copies of the judgment be supplied to both the parties.
